LESSON: WRITING 7.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING- DIALOGUE

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are interjections important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. write a simple dialogue on the theme using interjections
2. appreciate the need of creative writing

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 7.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING- DIALOGUE
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 7.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING- DIALOGUE
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Write a simple dialogue on the theme using interjections

What this means
In this part you learn to write a simple dialogue on the theme using interjections. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a simple dialogue on the theme using interjections.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a simple dialogue on the theme using interjections. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the need of creative writing

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the need of creative writing. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the need of creative writing.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the need of creative writing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: write a simple dialogue on the theme using interjections)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue to a partner. (skill: appreciate the need of creative writing)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: write a simple dialogue on the theme using interjections.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the need of creative writing.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are interjections important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: write a simple dialogue on the theme using interjections.
5. Be able to: appreciate the need of creative writing.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
